name: Amasiah
overview: Amasiah was a male military leader in the kingdom of Judah, known primarily as the son of Zichri. He served under King Jehoshaphat as a commander of 200,000 men, demonstrating a significant role in the defense and military organization of Judah. There is no additional information on his tribal affiliation or other personal notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Amasiah means 'Yahweh carries a load,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning tied to God's sustaining power. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries a clear reference to the divine.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Amasiah was the son of Zichri. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text regarding Amasiah.
scriptureSignificance: Amasiah's significance lies in his leadership role during King Jehoshaphat's reign, commanding a large army which underscores his trusted position in Judah's military hierarchy. His mention highlights the organized and sizable forces mobilized under Jehoshaphat's rule, reflecting the kingdom's strength and reliance on capable leaders. Through Amasiah, the narrative shows the importance of faithful and effective military leadership in the preservation and defense of God's people.
